blocks.prompt: Start by asking: what question am I trying to answer, and which data source gives the most direct evidence?

blocks.title: Log Data for Investigations exam shortcuts
items: Need to know if a connection was allowed or blocked → FIREWALL LOG
Example: Confirm whether TCP 443 from an external IP was permitted.
Need to investigate a failed app login or transaction → APPLICATION LOG
Example: Review failed login attempts in a web application.
Need process execution or host activity → ENDPOINT LOG
Endpoint telemetry shows what occurred on the device.
Example: EDR records PowerShell spawning a suspicious process.
Need Windows logon or OS audit event → OS SECURITY LOG
Operating-system security logs capture local authentication and audit events.
Example: Review Windows Security Event logs.
Need known exploit or scan detection → IDS/IPS LOG
IDS/IPS logs show signature or anomaly detections.
Example: An IDS detects repeated exploit attempts.
Need context without full content → METADATA
Metadata tells you about the event or object.
Example: Timestamp, source IP, destination IP, and file hash.
blocks.example: Choose the source that provides the most direct evidence for the investigation question.

questions.q: An investigator needs to confirm whether a firewall allowed or blocked traffic from a suspicious external IP. Which source is most useful?
questions.explanation: Firewall logs record traffic decisions such as allowed or blocked connections.

questions.q: A user reports repeated login failures in a web application. Which source should the analyst check first?
questions.explanation: Application logs record app-specific authentication, errors, and user activity.

questions.q: An analyst needs to determine which process executed PowerShell on a compromised laptop. Which source is most useful?
questions.explanation: Endpoint logs and EDR telemetry provide host-level process activity.

questions.q: An investigator needs Windows logon and local security audit events. Which source is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: OS-specific security logs contain operating-system audit and authentication events.

questions.q: A security team wants to determine whether an IDS detected a known exploit attempt. Which source is most direct?
questions.explanation: IDS/IPS logs record detected or blocked suspicious network activity.

questions.q: An investigator wants to review VPN connection events and DNS activity. Which source is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Network logs include telemetry from VPNs, DNS, routers, switches, and other infrastructure.

questions.q: An analyst only needs timestamp, source IP, destination IP, and file properties rather than full content. What type of information is this?
questions.explanation: Metadata is descriptive information about data or communications rather than the full content.
